description: SSH Config terminal manager based on Python and Click framework with Rich and Textual UI

summary.one_liner: A terminal manager for SSH config files that lists, filters, edits and groups hosts with a Click CLI (sshc) and a Textual browser (ssht).
summary.what_it_does: SSHClick parses an existing SSH config file (default ~/.ssh/config) and provides the sshc command to list, show, create, rename, set and delete hosts and groups. Groups and host metadata are stored as special comment lines (#@group, #@desc, #@info, #@host) so they stay readable in the config file and are parsed back by the tool. Several output styles are available for host display (panels, card, simple, table, table2, json), and settings can be stored in the config file via sshc config set. The companion ssht command opens a Textual TUI over the same parsed config, with a tree of groups and hosts, detail panes, and buttons or keys for ssh, sftp, key copy, editing and deleting. Top-level Include files are merged into a read-only view. Commands that only read (show, list) do not modify the file.
use_cases: Organize SSH hosts into named groups
Open ssh or sftp sessions from a terminal browser
Add, rename or delete SSH host entries from the command line
Back up and share SSH config with descriptions and notes embedded as comments
Display host lists in table or JSON form
how_to_run: git clone <repo-url> && cd sshclick && pip install .
notable: Stores groups and metadata as comment lines inside the existing SSH config, with no separate storage layer
Two entry points: sshc CLI and ssht Textual TUI sharing one parsed config model
Read-only merging of top-level Include files
Output styles including JSON for scripting, and ANSI codes stripped when writing to a file
Shell autocompletion for bash and zsh
caveats: Write commands rewrite the SSH config in SSHClick's own style, so comments outside its format may be lost
When Include is present, all modification and write-back is disabled
Only tested on Linux (Debian, Ubuntu); README says it should work elsewhere, including Windows and WSL
The TUI connectivity view is limited to graph/tunnel diagnostics; delete is unavailable in read-only mode
